name: Simple Winter Tips to Save on Heating Costs
titleTag: Save on Heating This Winter | HVA Climate Control
metaDescription: Looking to cut your heating bill this winter? These simple tips will help you save energy, stay warm, and keep your HVAC system running efficiently.
excerpt: Heating costs rising? These 5 simple tips will help you cut energy use, improve comfort, and keep your HVAC system running efficiently.
content:
Simple Winter Tips to Save on Heating Costs

When temperatures drop, your heating bill can climb fast. But with a few simple changes, you can stay warm without wasting energy or money. Here are some quick, effective ways to save on heating this winter:

1. Lower Your Thermostat at Night

Turning your thermostat down 7–10 degrees while you sleep can save up to 10% on annual heating costs, according to the U.S. Department of Energy.

2. Seal Drafts Around Doors and Windows

Use weather stripping or caulk to block cold air from seeping into your home. Even small gaps can drive up your heating bill.

3. Change Your Furnace Filter

A clean filter helps your system run more efficiently, reducing strain and improving airflow throughout your home.

4. Use a Programmable Thermostat

Set it to lower the temperature when you are not home and warm up just before you return.

5. Schedule a Heating Tune-Up

A quick maintenance check can catch issues before they become costly repairs.

name: AC Not Cooling? Try These 3 Quick Fixes First
titleTag: AC Not Cooling? 3 Fixes to Try | HVA Climate Control
metaDescription: AC not cooling your home? Before calling a pro, try these three quick fixes that solve the most common issues — fast, easy, and DIY-friendly.
excerpt: AC not cooling? Before you book a service call, try these 3 easy troubleshooting steps to potentially solve the issue yourself.
content:
If your air conditioner is running but not cooling your home, do not panic. There are a few simple things you can check before calling an HVAC professional.

1. Check the Thermostat Settings

Make sure your thermostat is set to cool and that the temperature is set lower than your current room temp.

2. Inspect the Air Filter

A dirty air filter can block airflow, causing the system to overheat or freeze up. Replace it if it looks dirty.

3. Look at the Outdoor Unit

Head outside and check the condenser unit. Clear away any debris like leaves, weeds, or dirt that might block airflow.

If you have tried all of the above and your AC still is not cooling, it may be a bigger issue. That is when it is time to call HVA Climate Control.

name: Why Is Your AC Blowing Warm Air?
titleTag: Why Is My AC Blowing Warm Air? | HVA Climate Control
metaDescription: Is your AC blowing warm air instead of cooling your home? Discover common causes and how to fix them before calling in a professional HVAC technician.
excerpt: If your air conditioner is running but blowing warm air, you might have a filter, coil, or refrigerant issue. Here is what to check first.
content:
Why Is Your AC Blowing Warm Air?

Nothing is worse than turning on the AC during a hot day only to feel warm air coming from your vents.

1. Incorrect Thermostat Settings

Double-check that your thermostat is set to cool and not just fan.

2. Dirty Air Filter

A clogged air filter restricts airflow and can cause your system to overheat.

3. Refrigerant Leak

Low refrigerant levels mean your system cannot absorb heat from inside your home. This usually requires professional repair.

4. Tripped Breaker or Blown Fuse

Sometimes the outdoor unit loses power, causing the inside unit to run without cooling.

5. Dirty Condenser Coils

The outdoor coils release heat from your home. If they are covered in dirt or debris, your AC will struggle to cool effectively.

When to Call a Pro

If you have checked the basics and it is still blowing warm air, call HVA Climate Control. We serve Vancouver, WA, and the surrounding areas with same-day service.

name: How Often Should You Replace Your Furnace Filter?
titleTag: How Often to Replace Your Furnace Filter | HVA Climate
metaDescription: Find out how often to change your furnace filter. Learn the signs, timelines, and benefits of replacement for a cleaner, more efficient HVAC system.
excerpt: Replacing your furnace filter regularly is key to energy efficiency, air quality, and HVAC system health. Here is how often you should do it.
content:
How Often Should You Replace Your Furnace Filter?

Replacing your furnace filter is one of the simplest yet most important HVAC maintenance tasks.

General Guidelines

  • Standard filters (1-2 inches thick): Every 1-3 months
  • Thicker filters (4-5 inches): Every 6-12 months
  • HEPA or high-efficiency filters: Check every 2 months

You should also consider: pets in the home, allergies or asthma, usage frequency, and local air quality.

Why It Matters

Neglecting your furnace filter can lead to reduced airflow, higher energy bills, poor indoor air quality, and unnecessary strain on your system.

At HVA Climate Control, we recommend checking your filter monthly. Our team proudly serves Vancouver, WA, and Portland, OR.
